content.text: Denying a quantifier flips it. 'Not every A is B' means some A is not B: ¬∀x φ is equivalent to ∃x ¬φ.
'No A is B' means every A is not B: ∀x(A(x) → ¬B(x)). That is equivalent to ¬∃x(A(x) ∧ B(x)).

examples.note: It is not true that all students are lazy. So some student is not.

question.hint: 'No A is B' says every A is not B.
question.explanation: For every x, if x is a philosopher, then x is not rich.
